# T-1: Split GUARDRAIL_EVAL_SCHEMA into article and requirement schemas

## Goal
Replace the shared schema with GUARDRAIL_ARTICLE_EVAL_SCHEMA (article path) and IMPL_REQUIREMENT_EVAL_SCHEMA (requirement path), both as JSON Schema objects on src/flow/lib/run-gate.js. Add named exports for both.

## Acceptance Criteria
- src/flow/lib/run-gate.js defines GUARDRAIL_ARTICLE_EVAL_SCHEMA with per-entry {guardrail_id, result, reason?, violations?: [{target, where, why_violates}]} and IMPL_REQUIREMENT_EVAL_SCHEMA with per-entry {guardrail_id, result, reason}.
- Both schemas reject extra properties at the entry level.
- GUARDRAIL_EVAL_SCHEMA constant is removed.
- Both schemas are added to the module's named exports.

## Implementation Notes
Place schema constants near the existing GUARDRAIL_EVAL_SCHEMA definition (around run-gate.js:619). Article schema's outer object has reason and violations as optional siblings (no oneOf). Inner violation schema requires target / where / why_violates as non-empty strings (string min-length is enforced by the parser, not the schema, to keep provider compatibility broad).

## Test Strategy
Unit test asserts the structural shape of each constant via JSON snapshot (or property-by-property assertions) and via export-presence assertions.
